prompt:
A line-art multi-panel storyboard of one continuous scene of a live-action short drama: one image divided into a grid of 3 columns and 2 rows of equal 9:16 panels, 5 panels read from left to right and top to bottom; cells after the last panel stay plain white. Every panel is a colouring-book drawing: contours only, in one thin uniform black line on white, most of the panel left white. Draw only the people and the few large shapes of the place (walls, doors, windows, a bed, a car). People are simple storyboard figures: hair is one smooth outline of its shape, like a cap, empty inside, with no strands, curls or waves; a face has one short line each for the eyes, brows, nose and mouth, and no stubble, wrinkles or jaw lines; a fence is its posts and top rail, a tree its outline. No texture, mesh, bricks, leaves or fabric folds; no shading, grey or solid black: dark hair, clothes and cars are outlines left white inside. Thin black panel borders, plain white gutters. Location: INT. JI RAN'S OFFICE, Day, soft daylight through the floor-to-ceiling windows.
Image 1: the character sheet of Ji Ran (27), look S0
Image 2: the location INT. JI RAN'S OFFICE, the front view, the establishing view, facing the back wall, with no people
Image 3: the location INT. JI RAN'S OFFICE, the back view, turned 180 degrees, facing the front wall, with the left wall at its right edge, with no people
Image 4: the location INT. JI RAN'S OFFICE, the left-side view, facing the left wall, with the back wall at its right edge, with no people
Image 5: the location INT. JI RAN'S OFFICE, the right-side view, facing the right wall, with the back wall at its left edge, with no people
Image 6: the location INT. JI RAN'S OFFICE, the floor plan seen from above: its top edge is the back wall, its bottom edge the front wall behind the front view's camera, and its left and right edges the left and right walls, with no people
Image 7: the blocking reference of this segment, the same place with its people in their places at the start; use it only for where each person is and which way they face, and keep each person on that seat or spot, on the same side of the room, in every panel until a shot moves them; do not copy its colours or light
Image 8: the prop pour-over coffee equipment; use only structure, material, and color
Draw each character so they can be told apart as in their reference image, by the shape of the hairstyle, the build and the outfit in outline only; never copy the photograph's detail. Use the character sheets only for the characters, not for their layout, white background or multiple views. Use the location images only for the layout of the space and the place of its furniture and props, drawn in outline. There is only one of each vehicle, piece of furniture and prop that the location shows, defined by the location images, throughout all panels; when a panel shows only part of one, such as a car's hood, it is that same object, and no second one appears. Each panel shows only the characters it names, and nobody appears twice in one panel.
At the start: Ji Ran stands behind the walnut executive desk in front of the floor-to-ceiling windows, facing the pin-up wall. She wears the dove-grey silk shirt and the black pencil skirt. The white coffee cup, now filled, sits on its saucer at the pour-over station beside the kettle, dripper and server. The plans, wood samples and metal figurine lie across the desktop, and the black leather chair stands behind her. Camera side: in front of the desk, on the pin-up wall side, facing the desk and the windows.
Panel 1: Medium close-up, slow push in, eye level, from the front of the desk. Ji Ran lifts the white cup and sips, her eyes distant and her lips on the rim.
Panel 2: Close-up insert, locked-off camera, high angle, over the pour-over station. Ji Ran's hand sets the cup back down firmly on its saucer.
Panel 3: Wide shot, locked-off camera, eye level, from the pin-up wall facing the desk and the windows. Ji Ran turns from the desk toward the floor-to-ceiling windows and the city skyline, her mouth closed.
Panel 4: Medium shot, locked-off camera, low angle, from the front of the desk. Ji Ran turns back toward the pin-up wall and plants both hands on the desk beside the plans.
Panel 5: Close-up, slow push in on her eyes, eye level, from the front of the desk. Ji Ran's gaze hardens into steely resolve, her lips pressed shut.
Keep the characters, the number and position of every vehicle, piece of furniture and prop, and the location's spatial orientation consistent across all panels.
No text, letters, numbers, captions, speech bubbles, panel labels or watermark anywhere in the image; no photographic rendering.
